chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Ibn Abi Umayr and Safwan from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When you depart for 'Arafah, say while heading towards it: 'O God, to You I have directed my gaze, and upon You I have relied, and I seek Your Face. I ask You to bless my journey, fulfill my need, and make me among those whom You boast about on this day before those who are superior to me.' Then enter the state of Ihram (Talbiyah) while heading to 'Arafat. When you reach 'Arafat, pitch your tent in Namira, which is the valley of 'Uranah, before the Station and before 'Arafah. When the sun sets on the Day of 'Arafah, perform ritual bath and pray Dhuhr and 'Asr with one Adhan and two Iqamas, for you are hastening 'Asr and combining them to free yourself for supplication, for it is a day of supplication and asking.
He said: The boundary of 'Arafah is from the valley of 'Uranah and Thawiyyah and Namira to Dhi al-Majaz, and behind the mountain is the Station (Mawqif).

key_terms.أَذَانٍ وَاحِدٍ وَإِقَامَتَيْنِ: One Adhan and two Iqamas, a method of combining prayers
key_terms.الْمَوْقِف: The Station, referring to the specific area of standing during Hajj
key_terms.تُلَبِّي: To enter the state of Ihram by reciting the Talbiyah
key_terms.ذِي الْمَجَاز: Dhi al-Majaz, a place near 'Arafah marking its boundary
key_terms.عَرَفَةَ: Arafah, the plain where the standing (wuquf) of Hajj takes place
key_terms.نَمِرَةَ: Namira, a specific location in 'Arafah where the Prophet pitched his tent

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended supplications and prayer methods for the Day of 'Arafah according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* details the specific Sunnahs of the Day of 'Arafah, emphasizing the strategic timing of combining Dhuhr and 'Asr prayers to maximize the window for supplication, a practice rooted in the Prophet’s tradition. It further clarifies the geographical boundaries of the standing place (Mawqif), noting that while Namira is the traditional tent site, the actual ritual standing extends to the valley of 'Urnah and surrounding areas, reflecting the scholarly consensus on the flexibility of the Mawqif's limits.
